shots.title: THE SAHARA WAS GREEN
shots.purpose: Open on the impossible image: a green Sahara with lakes and hippos
shots.claim: the Sahara hosted lakes and wetland fauna ~6,000 years ago
shots.evidence: full-bleed dawn lakescape plate; the water and the hippos are the subject
shots.motion_reason: slow push-in: the impossible scene lands clean before any science
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the rock-art panel when the proof is asked for

subject_contract.expected_subject: a dawn lakescape in a green Sahara: wide calm lake, hippopotamuses at the waterline, acacia trees
required: lake or water as a major element
hippopotamus visible at or in the water

one_second.relationship: hippos in a Sahara lake — the impossible image

shots.purpose: Show the physical record: the panels are still on the rock
shots.claim: 15,000+ rock-art panels across the Sahara record wetland life
shots.evidence: ochre rock-art plate: giraffes and figures on sandstone
shots.motion_reason: reveal across the panel face so the figures register in sequence
shots.transition_reason: cut to the then/now split for the contrast

subject_contract.expected_subject: ancient ochre rock art painted on a sandstone cliff face: giraffes and human figures
required: rock or cliff wall bearing painted or engraved figures

one_second.relationship: the giraffes on the rock — the record itself

shots.purpose: Then vs now: the same land, two states — green with water, cracked dry
shots.claim: African Humid Period: monsoon-fed lakes vs today's hyperarid core
shots.evidence: split plate: green wetland half vs cracked arid half
shots.motion_reason: gentle drift across the split so both states are read
shots.transition_reason: cut to the orbital diagram when the mechanism must be seen

subject_contract.expected_subject: a split composition: lush green wetland on one side, cracked bone-dry desert on the other
required: one side green with water and vegetation
other side arid: cracked earth or dunes

one_second.relationship: one land, two states — green and dry

shots.purpose: Make the switch visible: axial wobble dragging the monsoon north
shots.claim: axial precession (~26,000-year cycle) paces the North African monsoon
shots.evidence: parchment diagram plate: tilted Earth, axis line, wobble arrows, monsoon arrow
shots.motion_reason: slow zoom on the Earth so the wobble and the arrow read as one idea
shots.transition_reason: cut to the dry lakebed for the ending of the green age

subject_contract.expected_subject: a parchment-style scientific diagram: a tilted Earth with its axis drawn as a line, wobble arrows, and a monsoon wind arrow sweeping toward North Africa
required: a drawn Earth with an axis line

one_second.relationship: the wobbling Earth moving the monsoon

shots.purpose: Show the ending: the lakebed itself, dried within centuries
shots.claim: the humid period ended ~5,500 BP within centuries, driving migration to the Nile
shots.evidence: cracked dry lakebed plate where the lake once was
shots.motion_reason: slow drift over the cracks — emptiness carries the ending
shots.transition_reason: cut to the type card for the statement

subject_contract.expected_subject: a vast cracked dry lakebed where a lake once was, distant sand dunes, hazy sky

one_second.relationship: the dead lakebed — the green age is over

shots.purpose: State the claim bluntly: the type IS the visual
shots.claim: green Sahara episodes recur, paced by orbital cycles
shots.evidence: full-frame type card: IT WAS GREEN
shots.transition_reason: cut to the dust plume for the payoff

subject_contract.expected_subject: a full-frame typographic card: IT WAS GREEN with a small supporting line

shots.purpose: Land the payoff: the desert still feeds the green world — the link never cut
shots.claim: Saharan dust fertilizes the Amazon (~27 Mt/yr)
shots.evidence: satellite-style plate: orange dust plume crossing the Atlantic
shots.motion_reason: slow drift along the plume — motion across the ocean carries the link

subject_contract.expected_subject: satellite view of a vast orange dust plume drifting from the African coast across the Atlantic toward South America

one_second.relationship: the dust crossing the ocean — the link alive
